From Wiktionary, the free dictionary

English

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • Audio (Southern England):(file)

Noun

[edit]

remote control (countable and uncountable, plural remote controls)

  1. (countable) A device used to operate an appliance (such as a television, vehicle, or mechanical toy) from a short distance away.
    Hyponyms: buttons, channel changer, clicker, remote, zapper, channel flicker, flicker
    • 2011 December 15, Felicity Cloake, “How to cook the perfect nut roast”, in Guardian‎[1]:
      A single slice of this could leave you supine in front of the Queen's speech without even the wherewithal to reach for the remote control.
  2. (uncountable) A means of operating a device from a distance, such as radio control or wire-guided control.
    Synonym: telearchics
    The bomb was detonated by remote control.

Descendants

[edit]
  • → Japanese: リモートコントロール (rimōto kontorōru), リモートコントローラー (rimōto kontorōrā)
